s78: What's the difference between Dimout and Blackout?
s79: People tend to call every opaque fabric the same thing, but their light-blocking levels differ. Choose wrong and your bedroom won't get fully dark.

s82: What are Magic Screen (Zebra) blinds and who are they for?
s83: Roller blinds with alternating sheer and solid stripes that adjust light while keeping the view. Better for living rooms and workspaces than bedrooms that need real darkness.

s88: Wooden blinds vs aluminium blinds: picking the right one for each room
s89: Wood is warm and beautiful but dislikes moisture; aluminium is water-resistant but cooler in feel. A clear comparison of which material suits which room.
s90: Zip-track blinds vs outdoor roller blinds: how different is their rain protection?
s91: Standard tracks leave gaps for wind-driven rain; zip tracks seal the edges more tightly. But neither keeps out driving rain 100 percent.
s92: Window film and curtains: overlapping or truly complementary?
s93: Do you still need curtains once you have film? The two work at different points — they aren't duplicates. Check which your room needs.
s94: Can you wash curtains yourself? Check when to send them to a shop
s95: Most light sheers can be washed at home, but heavy fabrics with linings or blackout coatings risk damage if washed the wrong way. Check before you decide.
s96: PVC strip curtains for factories: how to choose for real value
s97: Plastic strip curtains aren't just clear strips in a row. Get the thickness, overlap or mounting point wrong and a factory will leak both cold air and dust.
s98: Wallpaper and curtains: how to pair them without clashing
s99: A busy wall plus busy curtains and the room fights itself. Pair tones and patterns so there's a single star, and the room instantly feels calmer and more upscale.
s100: Fabric printing and branded curtains: when is it worth it?
s101: Printing a logo on curtains isn't worth it for every project. Use it when a brand needs to show its identity clearly, or when the pattern you want can't be found on the market.
s102: 2026 curtain trends Thai homes actually use
s103: We filter global trends down to what Thai homes really choose: warm tones, layered curtains, motors where they matter, and fabrics that are easy to care for in humid weather.
s104: How to choose bedroom curtains for better sleep
s105: Bedrooms that don't get fully dark usually fail at the curtain edges and fabric type. Choose the right Blackout, then install it to truly cover the frame.
s106: Kitchens and bathrooms: choosing moisture-resistant curtains
s107: Steam is the enemy of heavy fabric curtains and wooden blinds. Wet zones should start with easy-to-wipe materials like aluminium or low-maintenance roller blinds.
s108: Small condos: choosing curtains that don't make the room feel cramped
s109: Hang heavy, dark curtains across a whole wall in a 28 sq m room and it shrinks instantly. Light tones, clean lines and hanging them higher really help.
s110: Homes with young children: choosing curtains with less risk
s111: Curtain cords and chains hanging within a child's reach are a common hazard. Cut down on hanging cords, choose cordless or motorized systems, and install out of reach — a practical place to start.
s112: How do S-Wave curtains differ from pinch-pleat curtains?
s113: Smooth waves versus dimensional pleats — different jobs, different looks. Compare clearly before cutting fabric for the whole house.
s114: Roman blinds: which windows do they suit?
s115: Roman blinds look beautiful when folded in layers, but they aren't worth it for every window. Check the window size and how often it's opened before cutting.
s116: Eyelet curtains vs pencil-pleat curtains: how to choose
s117: Eyelets give natural waves, pencil pleats give a warm look. The two hang on the rail in different ways. Check your room style before cutting.
s118: What's the difference between waterfall and Louis curtains?
s119: Two premium decorative styles with different fabric rhythms for different rooms. Compare clearly before spending on a valance.
s120: Motorized curtains: mains power vs battery
s121: Mains power needs no charging but requires a power point; battery is easy to install but needs recharging. Choose based on your home's situation first.
s122: Can motorized curtains connect to Google Home / Apple Home?
s123: Many models really can connect, but not every motor. Check your home system and connectivity standard before buying.
s124: Do solar-powered motorized curtains really work in Thai homes?
s125: They work if the window gets real sun. The solar panel tops up the battery, but it isn't free power all year for every window. Check the sun direction before buying.
s126: What is the Matter standard and what does it have to do with motorized curtains?
s127: Matter is a common language for smart homes that helps motorized curtains talk to Google and Apple more easily — if you choose a model that truly supports it.
s128: Musty-smelling curtains: how to fix them without washing every time
s129: Musty smells mostly come from moisture trapped in the fabric. Let air through and deal with damp spots first; washing the whole curtain comes later.
s130: Noisy, stiff curtain tracks: can you fix them yourself?
s131: Squeaks and stiff tracks mostly come from dust and worn runners. Check one point at a time before taking down the whole track.
s132: Curtains fading from the sun: how to prevent it
s133: Sun fades every fabric, just at different speeds. Prevent it through sun direction, fabric layers and film — don't wait until they fade to fix it.
s134: Curtains and pets: choosing fabric and installation
s135: Clinging fur, snagging claws, pee and torn hems — solve them with fabric type, length and installation, not just a colour that hides fur.
s136: Japanese, Euro or USA partitions: how to choose
s137: The three look similar, but differ clearly in translucency and zoning performance. Compare before choosing so you don't pay twice.
s138: Hospital/clinic curtains: what to look for
s139: Healthcare work isn't just about picking a nice fabric. Discuss standards with the facility before ordering — this article runs through the questions to ask.
s140: Ordering curtains for many units in a condo project: how it works
s141: Ordering unit by unit differs from ordering a whole floor. We walk through measuring, fabric samples and installation scheduling so the project runs smoothly.
s142: Office/shop curtains: which type is best?
s143: Offices and storefronts have different needs: light control, no screen glare, easy care. Choose what your team can handle using every day.
s144: How to match curtain colour with your walls without it looking off
s145: Curtain colour can throw off a whole room. Use monochrome, complementary and accent rules, then compare real fabric under your room's light before deciding.
s146: What are double-layer curtains and why do beautiful homes use them?
s147: Sheer plus blackout isn't just for show. It softens daylight, darkens the night and keeps the room's look — all in one set.
s148: Tall windows/skylights: which curtains to use
s149: Out-of-reach tall windows and roof skylights need different systems. Motors and skylight blinds help when chosen to fit the site.
s150: Can Japandi style work with curtains in Thai homes?
s151: Japandi is warm minimalism. Natural-toned textured fabrics really work in Thai homes, as long as you don't copy rooms from cold countries.
s152: Repairing curtain tracks/motors: how much can you DIY?
s153: Stiff tracks, unresponsive motors, unpaired remotes — tell apart what you can try yourself and what needs a technician before the whole set breaks.
s154: Replacing old curtains without replacing the track
s155: If the track is still good, you can save — as long as the new fabric fits the existing system. Make sure to check the track type, fabric weight and hooks before cutting.
s156: Cleaning blinds without taking them down
s157: Dusting slat by slat the right way helps a lot, and there are tools that really help. But ingrained stains or some wooden blinds still need special care.
s158: Caring for Magic Screen blinds so the stripes don't misalign
s159: Misaligned or creased sheer-solid stripes mostly come from pulling at the wrong moment and from moisture. Proper care keeps the stripes straight for longer.
s160: How motorized curtain prices are worked out vs manual curtains
s161: A motorized budget isn't just the motor — it includes track, electrical work, fabric and site conditions. Break it down before comparing with manual curtains.
s162: Curtaining the whole house on a small budget: how to prioritise
s163: You don't need to do every room at once. Prioritise bedrooms, sun-heavy rooms and show rooms; rarely used rooms can wait for phase two.
s164: Ready-made vs made-to-measure curtains: what's the difference?
s165: Store-bought curtains are quick, but on unusual windows they're often loose or short. Made-to-measure fits the window with the right fabric allowance — if measured accurately.
s166: Getting your home ready for the hot season: how much can curtains help?
s167: Curtains cut glare and built-up heat to a degree, but they aren't an air conditioner. Put curtain layers, film and partitions in the right places.
